reference.answer: There are various types of dialog nodes. These include the Welcome node, which greets users when interacting with the assistant, and the Anything else node, which provides responses for unrecognized user input. You can also create custom nodes by adding a condition that triggers the assistant to process the node. It is possible to create an intent that can be recognized when a customer asks to speak to someone. After defining the intent, you can add a root-level dialog node that conditions the intent.

retrieved_documents.text: Defining intents   Intents are purposes or goals that are expressed in a customer's input, such as answering a question or processing a bill payment. By recognizing the intent expressed in a customer's input, the Watson Assistant service can choose the correct dialog flow for responding to it.     Intent creation overview     * Plan the intents for your application.  Consider what your customers might want to do, and what you want your application to be able to handle on their behalf. For example, you might want your application to help your customers make a purchase. If so, you can add a buy_something intent. (The that is added as a prefix to the intent name helps to clearly identify it as an intent.) * Teach Watson about your intents.  After you decide which business requests that you want your application to handle for your customers, you must teach Watson about them. For each business goal (such as buy_something), you must provide at least 5 examples of utterances that your customers typically use to indicate their goal. For example, I want to make a purchase.  Ideally, find real-world user utterance examples that you can extract from existing business processes. The user examples should be tailored to your specific business. For example, if you are an insurance company, a user example might look more like this, I want to buy a new XYZ insurance plan.  The examples that you provide are used by your assistant to build a machine learning model that can recognize the same and similar types of utterances and map them to the appropriate intent.    Start with a few intents, and test them as you iteratively expand the scope of the application.       Creating intents     1. Open your dialog skill. The skill opens to the Intents page. 2. Select Create intent. 3. In the Intent name field, type a name for the intent.    * The intent name can contain letters (in Unicode), numbers, underscores, hyphens, and periods. * The name cannot consist of .. or any other string of only periods. * Intent names cannot contain spaces and must not exceed 128 characters. The following are examples of intent names:    * weather_conditions

Step 2: Answer questions about the restaurant   Add an intent that recognizes when customers ask for details about the restaurant itself. An intent is the purpose or goal expressed in user input. The General_About_You intent that is provided with the General content catalog serves a similar function, but its user examples are designed to focus on queries about the assistant as opposed to the business that is using the assistant to help its customers. So, you will add your own intent.     Add the about_restaurant intent     1. From the Intents tab, click Create intent.  ![Shows the the Create intent button on the Intents page.](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs-content/v1/content/417db917d18067d9dcc4cf2612564a9a87c3ddc8/assistant/images/gs-ass-intent-add.png) 2. Enter about_restaurant in the Intent name field, and then click Create intent.  ![Shows the #about_restaurant intent being added.](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs-content/v1/content/417db917d18067d9dcc4cf2612564a9a87c3ddc8/assistant/images/gs-ass-add-intent.png) 3. Add the following user examples:  Tell me about the restaurant i want to know about you who are the restaurant owners and what is their philosophy? What's your story? Where do you source your produce from? Who is your head chef and what is the chef's background? How many locations do you have? do you cater or host functions on site? Do you deliver? Are you open for breakfast? 4. Click the Close!

To create a dialogue, follow these steps:
1. Click the Dialog tab and then click Create dialog. When you open the dialog editor for the first time, the Welcome and Anything else nodes will be created for you.
2. To add more nodes, click the "More" icon on the Welcome node and select Add node below.
3. In the "If assistant recognizes" field, enter a condition that, when met, triggers your assistant to process the node. Typically, you want to add an intent as the condition.
4. Specify the condition and response for each node. The condition specifies the information that must be present in the user input for the node to be triggered, while the response is the utterance that your assistant uses to respond to the user.
5. Save your progress.
Remember, the dialogue matches intents (what users say) to responses (what the bot says back) and can ask for more details in a text response and create one or more child nodes to process the new input.

There are various types of dialog nodes. These include the Welcome node, which greets users when interacting with the assistant, and the Anything else node, which provides responses for unrecognized user input. You can also create custom nodes by adding a condition that triggers the assistant to process the node. It is possible to create an intent that can be recognized when a customer asks to speak to someone. After defining the intent, you can add a root-level dialog node that conditions the intent.

Intents are the purposes or goals expressed in a customer's input, such as answering a question or processing a bill payment. By recognizing the intent in a customer's input, the Watson Assistant service can choose the appropriate dialog flow to respond. Intents added from a content catalog are distinguishable from other intents by their names. Each intent name is prefixed with the content catalog name.

rag_history_before_turn.content: What are the different types of dialog nodes?

There are various types of dialog nodes. These include the Welcome node, which greets users when interacting with the assistant, and the Anything else node, which provides responses for unrecognized user input. You can also create custom nodes by adding a condition that triggers the assistant to process the node. It is possible to create an intent that can be recognized when a customer asks to speak to someone. After defining the intent, you can add a root-level dialog node that conditions the intent.
Whatar are intents?

Intents are the purposes or goals expressed in a customer's input, such as answering a question or processing a bill payment. By recognizing the intent in a customer's input, the Watson Assistant service can choose the appropriate dialog flow to respond. Intents added from a content catalog are distinguishable from other intents by their names. Each intent name is prefixed with the content catalog name.
How is it created?

To create a dialogue, follow these steps:
1. Click the Dialog tab and then click Create dialog. When you open the dialog editor for the first time, the Welcome and Anything else nodes will be created for you.
2. To add more nodes, click the "More" icon on the Welcome node and select Add node below.
3. In the "If assistant recognizes" field, enter a condition that, when met, triggers your assistant to process the node. Typically, you want to add an intent as the condition.
4. Specify the condition and response for each node. The condition specifies the information that must be present in the user input for the node to be triggered, while the response is the utterance that your assistant uses to respond to the user.
5. Save your progress.
Remember, the dialogue matches intents (what users say) to responses (what the bot says back) and can ask for more details in a text response and create one or more child nodes to process the new input.

In such cases, the differences might not be readily discernible from the default expressive tone. rag_history_before_turn.content: What are the different types of dialog nodes?

There are various types of dialog nodes. These include the Welcome node, which greets users when interacting with the assistant, and the Anything else node, which provides responses for unrecognized user input. You can also create custom nodes by adding a condition that triggers the assistant to process the node. It is possible to create an intent that can be recognized when a customer asks to speak to someone. After defining the intent, you can add a root-level dialog node that conditions the intent.
Whatar are intents?

Intents are the purposes or goals expressed in a customer's input, such as answering a question or processing a bill payment. By recognizing the intent in a customer's input, the Watson Assistant service can choose the appropriate dialog flow to respond. Intents added from a content catalog are distinguishable from other intents by their names. Each intent name is prefixed with the content catalog name.
How is it created?

To create a dialogue, follow these steps:
1. Click the Dialog tab and then click Create dialog. When you open the dialog editor for the first time, the Welcome and Anything else nodes will be created for you.
2. To add more nodes, click the "More" icon on the Welcome node and select Add node below.
3. In the "If assistant recognizes" field, enter a condition that, when met, triggers your assistant to process the node. Typically, you want to add an intent as the condition.
4. Specify the condition and response for each node. The condition specifies the information that must be present in the user input for the node to be triggered, while the response is the utterance that your assistant uses to respond to the user.
5. Save your progress.
Remember, the dialogue matches intents (what users say) to responses (what the bot says back) and can ask for more details in a text response and create one or more child nodes to process the new input.
Are those the only steps?
If there are additional steps, I am not aware of them as the provided documents do not contain any information about them.
Are dialogue skills necessary?

Yes. Dialog Skill contains the training data and dialog that your assistant uses to chat with customers. It is a container for all the artifacts that define a conversation flow. Customize your assistant by adding the necessary skills to satisfy your customers' goals.

The response might be the answer to a question such as Where can I get some gas? or the execution of a command, such as turning on the radio. The intent and entity might be enough information to identify the correct response, or the dialog might ask the user for more input that is needed to respond correctly. For example, if a user asks, Where can I get some food? you might want to clarify whether they want a restaurant or a grocery store, to dine in or take out, and so on. You can ask for more details in a text response and create one or more child nodes to process the new input.  The dialog is represented graphically in Watson Assistant as a tree. Create a branch to process each intent that you want your conversation to handle. A branch is composed of multiple nodes. rag_history_before_turn.content: What are the different types of dialog nodes?

There are various types of dialog nodes. These include the Welcome node, which greets users when interacting with the assistant, and the Anything else node, which provides responses for unrecognized user input. You can also create custom nodes by adding a condition that triggers the assistant to process the node. It is possible to create an intent that can be recognized when a customer asks to speak to someone. After defining the intent, you can add a root-level dialog node that conditions the intent.
Whatar are intents?

Intents are the purposes or goals expressed in a customer's input, such as answering a question or processing a bill payment. By recognizing the intent in a customer's input, the Watson Assistant service can choose the appropriate dialog flow to respond. Intents added from a content catalog are distinguishable from other intents by their names. Each intent name is prefixed with the content catalog name.
How is it created?

To create a dialogue, follow these steps:
1. Click the Dialog tab and then click Create dialog. When you open the dialog editor for the first time, the Welcome and Anything else nodes will be created for you.
2. To add more nodes, click the "More" icon on the Welcome node and select Add node below.
3. In the "If assistant recognizes" field, enter a condition that, when met, triggers your assistant to process the node. Typically, you want to add an intent as the condition.
4. Specify the condition and response for each node. The condition specifies the information that must be present in the user input for the node to be triggered, while the response is the utterance that your assistant uses to respond to the user.
5. Save your progress.
Remember, the dialogue matches intents (what users say) to responses (what the bot says back) and can ask for more details in a text response and create one or more child nodes to process the new input.
Are those the only steps?
If there are additional steps, I am not aware of them as the provided documents do not contain any information about them.
Are dialogue skills necessary?

Yes. Dialog Skill contains the training data and dialog that your assistant uses to chat with customers. It is a container for all the artifacts that define a conversation flow. Customize your assistant by adding the necessary skills to satisfy your customers' goals.
What is the difference with the dialog node?

The dialog node response is similar to a Then statement in If-Then-Else programming logic. A skill performs the work of the assistant. A dialog skill contains the training data and dialog that your assistant uses to communicate with customers.

rag_history_before_turn.content: What are the different types of dialog nodes?

There are various types of dialog nodes. These include the Welcome node, which greets users when interacting with the assistant, and the Anything else node, which provides responses for unrecognized user input. You can also create custom nodes by adding a condition that triggers the assistant to process the node. It is possible to create an intent that can be recognized when a customer asks to speak to someone. After defining the intent, you can add a root-level dialog node that conditions the intent.
Whatar are intents?

Intents are the purposes or goals expressed in a customer's input, such as answering a question or processing a bill payment. By recognizing the intent in a customer's input, the Watson Assistant service can choose the appropriate dialog flow to respond. Intents added from a content catalog are distinguishable from other intents by their names. Each intent name is prefixed with the content catalog name.
How is it created?

To create a dialogue, follow these steps:
1. Click the Dialog tab and then click Create dialog. When you open the dialog editor for the first time, the Welcome and Anything else nodes will be created for you.
2. To add more nodes, click the "More" icon on the Welcome node and select Add node below.
3. In the "If assistant recognizes" field, enter a condition that, when met, triggers your assistant to process the node. Typically, you want to add an intent as the condition.
4. Specify the condition and response for each node. The condition specifies the information that must be present in the user input for the node to be triggered, while the response is the utterance that your assistant uses to respond to the user.
5. Save your progress.
Remember, the dialogue matches intents (what users say) to responses (what the bot says back) and can ask for more details in a text response and create one or more child nodes to process the new input.

If there are additional steps, I am not aware of them as the provided documents do not contain any information about them.

Yes. Dialog Skill contains the training data and dialog that your assistant uses to chat with customers. It is a container for all the artifacts that define a conversation flow. Customize your assistant by adding the necessary skills to satisfy your customers' goals.
What is the difference with the dialog node?

The dialog node response is similar to a Then statement in If-Then-Else programming logic. A skill performs the work of the assistant. A dialog skill contains the training data and dialog that your assistant uses to communicate with customers.

You have the option to add a conversational dialog and a search skill.

reference.answer: When Watson Assistant can't provide a direct solution, it uses a search skill to find an answer from your various self-service content sources. The search skill works with IBM Watson® Discovery service to extract information from a designated data collection. By creating a search skill, you'll receive a free instance of Discovery. After setting up the search, you can test it by sending queries and preview the results in the search skill's Preview pane.
